A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EVT research and contain 11 complete, readable pages. Text and rendered-page comparison supports assessment of all scientific content. Both end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: v3 reports original nuScenes detection results and component ablations in Tables 1–6, including experiments integrating geometry-aware cross-attention into StreamPETR.

after.justification: v4 retains the original nuScenes results, component ablations, and StreamPETR experiments reported in v3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain identical adaptive sampling/projection, group-wise mixed query selection, and geometry-aware cross-attention procedures.

E1.justification: Both use the same nuScenes coverage, including LiDAR-camera detection, LiDAR-only evaluation, and the camera-only StreamPETR experiment. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Figure 1 and Tables 1–6, including the benchmark detectors, query-initialization alternatives, attention variants, and StreamPETR baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain the same dataset splits, NDS/mAP metrics, backbone configurations, 10-epoch EVT training, 24/90-epoch StreamPETR experiments, and FP32 A100 timing protocol.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 retains all analyses of ASAP components, query initialization, attention components, StreamPETR integration, and first-layer query formulation. The sampling-point and BEV-feature visualizations are also identical.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–6 and the plotted and qualitative results are unchanged. Table 1 reports the same EVT test performance of 75.3% NDS and 72.6% mAP in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and method equations (1)–(19) are identical. Neither version adds or removes theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about detection accuracy, efficiency, LiDAR-guided view transformation, and improved query decoding.

C2.justification: Both retain identical interpretations of geometric alignment, shared query embeddings, and attention mixing, including the unsuccessful alternative initial bounding-box formulations discussed with Table 6. No limitation or applicability qualification changes.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures are identical, including sampling/query counts, architecture dimensions, losses, optimizer settings, augmentation, and training on eight RTX 3090 GPUs. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, citation usage, and all 60 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 removes 'Seoul' from both institutional affiliations and updates the arXiv margin stamp from v3, 26 March 2025, to v4, 11 July 2025. The scientific prose and document structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The shortened affiliation line is recentered on page 1. Figures 1–5, Tables 1–6, their captions and placement, and all subsequent page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The only visible revisions concern the affiliation line and version/date stamp. The scientific text, equations, experiments, results, and supporting displays are unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
